findings.title: The Layer 1 gate ignores the 2y and expected-path signals v2 just added, so the Fed-hike weeks read '무판정' (no verdict) and count as green
findings.location: 계층 1 > 의미 있는 4주 변화의 기준; 판정 절차 step 1; 결론 규칙 L1 green list
findings.problem: Step 1 only checks whether |Δ10y| ≤ 20bp and |ΔBE| ≤ 15bp. DGS2 is listed as 'direct observation of the policy path' (정책 경로를 직접 관측) and has its own ±20bp threshold, and the ACM expected path has ±15bp, but no step uses either. When the term premium falls while the policy path jumps, the 10y stays inside ±20bp and Layer 1 outputs 무판정 (no verdict), which maps to green. This is the exact regime v2 was built to catch.
findings.evidence: Computed with GSW and ACM data, Friday weeks, 4-week changes. Week of 9/11: 10y +20bp (exactly at the gate, so 무판정), 2y +50bp, ACM expected path +32bp, TP -13bp. Week of 9/18 (FOMC hike on 9/16): 10y +18, 2y +57, expected path +37, TP -20, so also 무판정 and green. Layer 1 first leaves green on 9/25. Since 2004, 69 of 640 무판정 weeks had |Δ2y| > 20bp, and 17 had > 35bp. Overall 54% of weeks are 무판정. The threshold table cites the 80th percentile as its basis (근거), but the 20bp nominal threshold is actually the 64th percentile of |4w change|; the 80th is 29bp. With FRED DGS10 (par yields), the 9/11 value may land 1-2bp on either side of the gate.
findings.fix: Pass the gate if any of these holds: |Δ10y| > 20, |Δ2y| > 20, |ΔACM expected path| > 15, or |ΔBE| > 15. Add explicit rows for 'nominal → but 2y or expected path ↑ = policy tightening (yellow)' and 'policy easing' for ↓. Either correct the basis column (nominal 20bp ≈ 64th percentile) or raise the nominal threshold to 25-30bp.

findings.title: The decomposition ① driver depends on the model half the time, and the current 4-week label flips under Kim-Wright
findings.location: 계층 1 판정 절차 step 2; 지표표 THREEFYTP10 row; 현재 판정; 이 대시보드가 하지 않는 것
findings.problem: Step 2 names whichever of expected path or TP has the larger |Δ|, with no minimum size and no margin. The KW cross-check only flags opposite direction. ACM and KW split the same yield move very differently (the standard deviation of KW's 4w TP changes is 0.53× ACM's), so the 'driver', and sometimes the light colour, is set by model choice. The doc also never says what '보류' (on hold) does to the Layer 1 light that feeds the sizing table.
findings.evidence: Computed, with KW downloaded from federalreserve.gov feds200533.csv (data through 10/9). Since 2004, ACM and KW pick a different ① driver in 274 of 549 weeks that get a verdict (50%). v2's 'directions disagree' rule would flag only 24 of those. The resulting light colour differs in 62 of 549 (11%). Current 4w (9/11 to 10/9): ACM gives TP +19 vs expected path +9, so '재정·공급·불확실성 프리미엄' (fiscal/supply/uncertainty premium). KW gives TP +11 vs expected path +15, so '긴축 재가격' (tightening repricing). The headline 'transitioning from tightening repricing to term-premium widening' therefore depends on the model. In 25% of weeks with a verdict, both ACM components sit below their own thresholds; the current 4w is one of them (TP +19 < 20, expected path +9 < 15), yet a driver is still named. Between consecutive weeks with a verdict, the driver flips 18% of the time.
findings.fix: Name a driver only if (a) it exceeds its own threshold, (b) it beats the other component by at least 1.5× or 10bp, and (c) ACM and KW agree. Otherwise label it '혼합' (mixed) and map it to yellow. Define '보류' as yellow, never green. Record both models' splits on the form. Note that KW comes directly from federalreserve.gov, so FRED is not needed.

findings.title: The worked example applies bucket rules to the wrong dates and metrics, and lights have no as-of or hold rule
findings.location: 결론 규칙 > 규칙 적용 예시 (10월 13~14일); 버킷 신호등 기준
findings.problem: The doc never says whether a bucket light is judged on today's close or holds for some days after a trigger. The example fills that gap differently for each bucket: one uses a 3-week-old reading, one uses an 8-week metric that is not in the rule, and one uses a trough-to-date window instead of 20 days.
findings.evidence: Recomputed on 10/13 closes. Rate volatility: MOVE 5d -3.9%, ^TYX 20d +19.9bp, ^TYX 5d -7.8bp, MOVE 101, so green by rule. v2 says yellow, citing the 9/24 +37% from 14 business days earlier. By v2's own red rule, rate volatility was red on 9/28 (^TYX 5d +26.5bp with MOVE 5d +25%) and on 9/29 (+29.1bp with +36%), which the doc never mentions; the last yellow trigger was 10/5 (^TYX 20d +41.9bp). Funding and dollar: the provisional yellow rests on 'DXY 8주 +4.1%' (DXY up 4.1% over 8 weeks), which is not a rule metric. DXY 20d is +2.5%, below +3%, so green until NFCI is checked. SOFR-IORB on 10/13 was -1bp (SOFR 3.89 from the NY Fed API; IORB taken as top of range minus 10bp = 3.90), so the red condition is not met. Credit: the '+20%' runs from the 8/28 trough to 10/12 (31 business days), not a 20-day change. The proxies over 9/15 to 10/13 are HYG/IEI -0.84% and HYGH -0.74%. The final 방어 (defensive) verdict survives (Layer 1 red + hedge red + A valid to 10/16), but the example teaches look-back cherry-picking.
findings.fix: Add one rule: each light is judged on the latest close and stays on for N trading days after a trigger (for example 10, matching the alarms), or for none. Rewrite the example table with each bucket's rule metric, its exact value and an as-of date, and note the 9/28-29 red episode.

findings.title: The evaluation clock is undefined, the daily list leaves out alarm inputs, and the state whipsaws
findings.location: 실행 루틴; 계층 2 '매일, 5분'; 결론 규칙 (한 단계씩 올림)
findings.problem: Bucket thresholds use rolling 5-day changes (MOVE 5d +20%, ^TYX 5d +25bp), but the routine refreshes lights only at the weekend, which brings back the Friday-sampling miss v2 claims to fix. The doc never says whether the sizing state is computed daily or weekly. The daily list (HYG/IEI, MOVE, VIX/VIX3M, ^TYX, DXY) leaves out TLT, which both A and B need, and the VIX level, which B needs; VIX/VIX3M is not an alarm input at all. Precedence between the 중립 (neutral) and 방어 (defensive) conditions is only implied, and the one-step-up rule has no minimum dwell time.
findings.evidence: Computed a daily reconstruction for 2006-2026. It omits the credit, NFCI, SOFR and crypto buckets, so it is a lower bound on reds. Evaluated daily, the state changes about 25 times a year (30 in 2025), and 30 of 80 방어 spells since 2008 lasted under 5 trading days. A weekly-review variant (Friday evaluation, immediate downgrade when A or B fires) gives 14 changes a year.
findings.fix: Write it down explicitly. A script evaluates all lights and A/B every trading day on closes. Downgrades take effect immediately. Upgrades happen only at the weekend review and only after the better state's conditions have held for at least 5 trading days. 방어 takes precedence. The daily list becomes HYG, IEI, TLT, MOVE, DXY and VIX (for A/B) plus ^TYX and VIX3M (for the buckets).

findings.title: The hedge bucket and the Layer 1 red rule are level states that stay on in this regime, which conflicts with principle 2
findings.location: 버킷 신호등 기준 (헤지 작동); 결론 규칙 L1 빨강 조건; 설계 원칙 2
findings.problem: Principle 2 says markets adapt to levels and speed is what breaks them. Yet two of the six counted buckets turn red on levels that persist for quarters, so in practice the 공격 (offensive) state is unreachable for most of 2026.
findings.evidence: Computed. S&P-TLT 63-day correlation in 2026: red on 63% of days, yellow 35%, green 2% (2025: red 6%, yellow 63%, green 31%). The 10y real rate (GSW) has been at or above the 94th percentile of its trailing 3 years every week since July 2026, so any yellow Layer 1 verdict is automatically red. Reconstructed 2026 state: 중립 66%, 방어 17%, 공격 18%. These reds do carry risk information: on 방어 days since 2008, P(63-day max drawdown < -10%) was 24% vs 12% on 공격 days. But a light that is almost always on cannot move the state.
findings.fix: Make 헤지 작동 (hedge working) a modifier rather than a counted red: when the correlation is above 0, stop counting Treasuries as the hedge. Or make it change-based, for example the 63-day correlation rising more than 0.4 in 3 months. For the Layer 1 red, use speed (real-rate 20-day z ≥ +1.5) or require both ≥ 99th percentile and rising.

findings.title: The alarm statistics quoted belong to a different rule than the one the doc tells you to run, and holiday rows create phantom alarms
findings.location: 계층 2 > 복합 경보 A형/B형 blocks; 유효 기간
findings.problem: The quoted results (12 weeks, -5.7%, 42%; 23 weeks) come from Friday-to-Friday weekly signals. v2 operates a daily rolling 5-business-day rule with 10-business-day validity, which fires far more often and has a weaker edge. The calendar is also undefined: load()'s ffill keeps weekday market-holiday rows, which shortens the 5-day window.
findings.evidence: Computed the daily rolling rule from 2008 to 10/13. A: 46 firing days in 19 episodes. B: 109 days in 36 episodes. Measured from episode starts, the 63-day S&P max drawdown median is -4.7% for A vs -3.0% unconditional, with P(<-10%) 33% vs 15%. For B the median is -3.0% (the same as unconditional) and P(<-10%) is 25% vs 15%. A or B is valid on 15.6% of days. Phantom alarm: B 'fired' only on 2026-02-16 (Presidents' Day). That row is forward-filled, so the window covers just 4 trading days; the real trading days 2/13 and 2/17 did not fire. On a trading-day calendar, B never fires in 2026, yet under the 10-day validity rule this phantom would mean two weeks in 방어. The doc also leaves the calendar (NYSE vs SIFMA; the bond market was closed on 10/12) and whether day 0 counts unstated.
findings.fix: Re-run the backtest on the exact daily rule and quote episodes rather than weeks. Drop non-trading rows (NYSE calendar) before differencing. Define '10영업일' as the 10 NYSE trading days after the firing day.

findings.title: The current-value block mixes pre-open snapshots with the previous day's closes
findings.location: 계층 2 > 표시 방식; 규칙 적용 예시; 데이터 소스 메모
findings.problem: yahoo.csv was downloaded at 13:28 UTC on 10/14 (09:28 ET, before the US open). load() forward-fills the ETF columns, so the last row is a hybrid. The displayed values, percentiles and z-scores come from that hybrid row, and a daily run at the wrong hour would feed intraday MOVE and stale ETF closes into the composite alarm.
findings.evidence: The raw 10/14 row has prints only for ^MOVE 96.65, ^TYX 5.621, ^VIX 15.80 (extended-hours value), DXY 102.835 and BTC; HYG, TLT and ^GSPC are NaN and get filled with 10/13 values. Display vs 10/13 close: 30Y '5.62%, 99, z +1.2, +27bp' vs close 5.563%, 98.7, +0.86, +19.9bp. MOVE '97, 58, +1.1, +16' vs 101.1, 67.7, +1.24, +17.4. The VIX/VIX3M row pairs 10/13's 0.85 with a percentile of 53 and z of -0.2 that belong to the hybrid 0.88; 0.85 itself is the 28th percentile with z -0.47. S&P-TLT '+0.45' includes a fake zero-return day; the 10/13 value is +0.425. 'DXY +4.1%' is +3.4% on closes. 'VIX 15.8' is 15.27 at the close. 30Y closing high: 5.665% on 10/5.
findings.fix: Use closes only and run after 07:00 KST. Drop the last row unless every required series has a print for that date (no forward-fill on the final row). Show the as-of date for each series in the display and on the record form.

findings.title: The claim that every case lands in one cell is false, and several rule inputs are undefined
findings.location: 판정 절차 last paragraph; 판정표: 명목금리 하락 시; 명목금리가 움직이지 않을 때; 현재 판정 (8주); 버킷과 지표 lead sentence
findings.problem: Some weeks have no Layer 1 cell, so the sizing input is undefined. The '8주 판정' (8-week verdict) used in the current reading and in the sizing example is not a defined procedure. The rule that each bucket has one representative indicator (대표 지표 하나만) contradicts thresholds that also use the auxiliary indicators (CCC-BB, ^TYX, DTWEXBGS, SOFR-IORB). 'S&P' never says which series. The z-score is displayed and recorded but no rule uses it.
findings.evidence: Computed since 2004: 109 of 1189 weeks (9.2%) fall in no cell. In 91 of them the 10y is within ±20bp and BE is outside ±15bp, but the real rate is within ±20bp, while the flat-nominal table needs the real rate ↑ or ↓. In the other 18 the rate is falling, the drivers are expected path × real, and S&P is →; that table defines only S&P ↑ and ↓. The 8-week verdict applies 4-week thresholds to a 37-business-day window. Its rates end on 10/9 while its S&P +1.3% ends on 10/14; the 10/9 value is +1.34%, so it happens to be harmless here.
findings.fix: Add the missing cells. With nominal flat: BE↑ and real → = rising inflation expectations (yellow); BE↓ and real → = disinflation (green). Falling, expected path × real, S&P → = waiting for confirmation (yellow). Drop the 8-week verdict, or define it with thresholds scaled by √2. Replace the 대표 지표 sentence with 'a light is set only by the conditions in the threshold table'. Specify ^GSPC (price index). Either use the z-score in a rule or label it as display-only.

findings.title: The crypto 7th bucket has no thresholds, and its data path breaks on US-hosted automation
findings.location: 계층 3; 결론 규칙 (7번째 버킷); 기록 양식 계층 3
findings.problem: The sizing rule adds a crypto leverage bucket (funding rate and open interest) for crypto exposure but never defines green, yellow or red for it. '경보 발동 시 매일' (daily when an alarm fires) does not say which alarm.
findings.evidence: Checked from this environment. Binance futures endpoints (fundingRate, openInterestHist) return HTTP 451 'restricted location', so any US-hosted runner such as GitHub Actions or a cloud session fails. Coinglass v4 returns 401 'API key missing'. The DefiLlama stablecoin API returns 200. To my knowledge, Binance documents openInterestHist as covering only the latest 30 days, so OI/market-cap percentiles need history you archive yourself.
findings.fix: Either exclude the 7th bucket from the count until about 6 months of archived data exist, or set provisional thresholds labelled as hypotheses (for example, 7-day average annualised funding > 20% yellow and > 40% red; OI/market cap 1-year percentile ≥ 80 yellow and ≥ 95 red). Start archiving now. Run crypto pulls from a Korean or local machine, or use other public exchange APIs. Name the alarm that triggers daily checks.

findings.title: The manual routine is not feasible: it needs automation, and the doc must specify dividend-adjusted prices
findings.location: 실행 루틴; 계층 2 '매일, 5분'; 기록 양식
findings.problem: The 5-minute daily check and the 20-30 minute weekend routine cannot be done reliably by hand. Broker apps show unadjusted prices, which bias the HYG/IEI and TLT triggers around ex-dividend dates.
findings.evidence: The daily A/B check needs 6 series × 2 dates = 12 lookups, plus counting 5 trading days back across holidays, plus ratio math. The bucket lights add ^TYX 5d and 20d, MOVE 5d and VIX/VIX3M. The weekend routine needs 3-year percentiles, 20-day z-scores, a 63-day correlation and parsing the ACM xls, which is not doable by hand in 20-30 minutes. From 3 years of Yahoo dividends (computed): HYG pays about 0.49% a month, IEI 0.28%, TLT 0.36%, with ex-dates around the 1st business day. On 24% of days the 5-day window contains an ex-date. On those days the unadjusted HYG/IEI 5-day change is lower by about 0.21pp (42% of the -0.5% trigger), and TLT by about 0.36pp (36% of ±1%). By-hand readings therefore lean toward A and away from B around each month start.
findings.fix: Make automation the default. A daily script reusing load() from analysis/verify_v1.py prints a one-screen status. Keep only FINRA, rating events and the 4-D checklist manual. State that all inputs are dividend-adjusted closes. The record form becomes the script output plus a one-line rationale.

findings.title: Publication lags are missing, the dollar trigger uses a weekly series, and the SOFR-IORB rule is too sensitive
findings.location: 데이터 소스 메모; 버킷과 지표 (자금·달러); 버킷 신호등 기준
findings.problem: The doc does not record publication cadence or lags, so the weekend routine and the lights silently use stale data. The dollar trigger uses DTWEXBGS, which is published weekly, while the alarms use daily DXY. The SOFR-IORB red rule (positive for 5 business days in a row) fires on routine repo pressure.
findings.evidence: Checked headers. The GSW nominal, GSW TIPS and Kim-Wright CSVs were last modified Tuesday 10/13 at 19:00 GMT, with data through Friday 10/9. If that weekly Tuesday cadence holds, a Saturday review only sees data through the previous Friday, which is why FRED's daily DGS and DFII series matter. The ACM xls at 13:28 UTC on 10/14 ended on 10/9. NFCI is weekly (published Wednesday, with past values revised) and DTWEXBGS is weekly via the H.10 release; this part is from general knowledge and not re-checked. SOFR-IORB, computed from the NY Fed API with IORB assumed at top of range minus 10bp: the red condition held on 58 of 397 days since 3/2025, continuously from Oct 20 to Dec 23 2025 and again on Jan 2-6 and Feb 20 to Mar 5 2026. With a > +5bp threshold it holds on 13 days. The current value is -1bp.
findings.fix: Add a cadence and lag column to the data source memo and an as-of date per series on the form. Use DXY 20d, or both measures, for the dollar trigger. Change the red rule to SOFR-IORB > +5bp for 5 days, or use standing repo facility take-up.

findings.title: Single points of failure and redistribution limits bear directly on the artifact-vs-web-page choice
findings.location: 데이터 소스 메모 (and the publishing format)
findings.problem: MOVE and every ETF close come only from Yahoo's unofficial v8 endpoint. MOVE drives two buckets and both composite alarms. ICE BofA and MOVE data carry redistribution limits that matter if the dashboard becomes a public page.
findings.evidence: Fallbacks checked as reachable: Cboe's free CSVs for VIX and VIX3M (data through 10/13) and VXTLT. VXTLT's 5-day changes correlate 0.70 with MOVE's since 2015, but only 230 of 383 MOVE ≥ +10% days also had VXTLT ≥ +10%, so it works as a fallback only with recalibrated thresholds. Licensing: FRED's ICE BofA series notes carry ICE's notice that reproduction is prohibited without permission (I could not re-check this because FRED is blocked here). MOVE is an ICE index, and Yahoo's terms cover personal use.
findings.fix: Keep the dashboard private (claude.ai artifacts are private by default), or publish only derived lights and z-scores with links to the source. Add a fallback order: Yahoo, then Cboe, then Stooq. Archive the raw pulls locally every day.

findings.title: Secondary or proxy-derived numbers are stated as primary facts
findings.location: 계층 2 notes (L144, L159); 현재 판정 수준; 계층 3 table; 데이터 소스 메모; 설계 원칙 6
findings.problem: Several numbers come from secondary sources or proxy series but are written as if they were primary FRED facts.
findings.evidence: 'FRED ICE BofA 최근 3년치만' (FRED provides only the last 3 years of ICE BofA data) is stated as fact twice (L159, L411), while the review's appendix lists it as a secondary, unverified source (datasetiq). 'HY OAS 약 64bp' at L144 is secondary and unlabelled. '실질 2.93%, 2008년 12월 이후 최고' (real 2.93%, highest since Dec 2008) is the GSW zero-coupon TIPSY10, not DFII10. The 2y moves +66/+16 are ACM-fitted ACMY02; GSW 2y gives +65/+16, so they are fine but should be labelled. The BTC-dollar correlation was computed with DXY, yet the table cites DTWEXBGS. On the term premium, ACM 0.90 is the highest since 2014-07, but KW 1.07 is the highest since 2010-04, so the models differ even on level rank. Principle 6, checked: there were 7 S&P closing drawdowns of 10% or more from all-time highs since 2011; TLT rose in 5 of them (2025 only +0.8%) and fell in 2 (2018-02, 2022). The claim is supported, but the count should be cited.
findings.fix: Tag each number with its source type: primary, secondary, or GSW/ACM stand-in. Change DTWEXBGS to DXY in that correlation, or recompute it on DTWEXBGS.

findings.title: The record form and display do not capture the inputs that actually trigger lights
findings.location: 기록 양식; 표시 방식
findings.problem: The form records levels, percentiles and 20-day z-scores, but the triggers are change measures that the form never records, so the form cannot reproduce how a light was set.
findings.evidence: The triggers are HY OAS 20d %, CCC-BB 20d bp, MOVE 5d %, ^TYX 5d/20d bp, NFCI 4-week change, broad dollar 20d %, the SOFR-IORB run length and the four A/B component values. The form has no MOVE 5d %, no HY OAS 20d %, no dollar 20d %, no A/B component values and no as-of dates; the z-score it records feeds no rule. The display shows the MOVE change in points while the rules use %. Unit wording is inconsistent: '5일' 6 times vs '5영업일' 7 times, '20일' 14 times vs '20영업일' 5 times.
findings.fix: Use one row per bucket: trigger value | threshold | light | as-of date. Add one A/B line listing the four component values. Use '영업일' (business days) wording everywhere.

findings.title: The document is hard to use on a phone: the verdict is buried and aligned blocks wrap
findings.location: Whole document (structure)
findings.problem: The document is 433 lines (about 14.9k characters). Page 1 is the v1 changelog table. The actionable verdict sits about 78% of the way down, and dated readings are mixed into the stable rules.
findings.evidence: Computed. The 방어 verdict is at line ~336. 35 of 58 code-block lines are wider than 40 display columns (max 83), so the display block and record form lose their alignment on a phone. The longest table cell is 179 display columns: the rising-rate expected path × real cell, which packs three S&P sub-cases. Dated items such as 'valid until 10/16' and the 10/9 verdict go stale within days.
findings.fix: Page 1: an auto-generated status card showing the state, red and yellow lights with as-of dates, alarm expiry, 2-3 next triggers and the last update time. Page 2: the sizing table, thresholds and A/B rules. Page 3: the Layer 1 steps, with the three-sub-case cell split into rows. Appendices: rationale, v1 changelog, record form and data sources. Replace code-block layouts with tables or cards. This favours a web page with collapsible sections over one long scrolling document.

findings.title: Some Korean sentences are unclear or misleading
findings.problem: A few sentences mislead, contradict another section, or are hard to parse, and BE is never spelled out.
findings.evidence: L159: 'FRED의 ICE BofA 시리즈는 2026년 4월부터 최근 3년치만 제공' reads as 'data starting April 2026'. L336: 'A형이 다시 발동하지 않아도 10월 16일 이후 빨강이 1개 이하로 줄어들어야 중립으로' stacks two conditions confusingly. Define BE at first use as 'BE(브레이크이븐 기대인플레이션)'. Split L90 into rows. Add ±3% to the 4-C rows. State the crypto counts explicitly, for example '크립토는 7개 중 빨강 0·노랑 1 이하 = 공격'.

verdicts.reason: Recomputed from GSW and ACM data with Friday 4-week changes. 9/11: 10y +19.9bp, BE +2.9 (no verdict), 2y +49.6, expected path +32.1, TP -13.4. 9/18: +18.5 / -7.9 / +56.7 / +37.3 / -20.4, also no verdict. The 9/25 week is the first verdict ('caution', red because real-rate pct ≥95). Since 2004: 640 of 1189 weeks get no verdict (54%), 69 of those had |Δ2y|>20 and 17 had >35, and 85 had |Δexpected path|>15. 20bp sits at the 64th percentile; the 80th is 29.4. The problem is real. Without the miss, the counterfactual L1 light for 9/14-9/25 would have been red. With hedge already red (97% of days since July), that moves the state to 방어 about two weeks earlier. Nothing else in the system caught 9/11-9/22 (rate-vol stayed green until 9/24). I downgrade from critical: the blind spot hits about 3 weeks a year, the fix is one line, and the doc does print 29bp next to 20bp, so the basis is not hidden, only unexplained.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Gate on |Δ10y|>20 OR |ΔBE|>15 OR |ΔACM expected path|>15 (2y is about 0.9 correlated with expected path, so one of the two is enough). Add a flat-nominal row: 'expected path ↑ beyond threshold = policy tightening (yellow)', and the ↓ counterpart. Add a sentence explaining why thresholds sit below the 80th-percentile basis, or rename the column to say 'reference'.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with feds200533.csv (THREEFYTP1000.B; KW expected path = THREEFY1000.B minus TP) from federalreserve.gov, Last-Modified 10/13. Of 549 verdict weeks, the driver differs in 274 (50%; 206 of these are weeks where nominal is outside ±20bp, so the driver actually matters). The v2 opposite-direction rule flags 54 weeks, 24 of them among the driver splits. The light differs in 63 weeks (reviewer: 62). The KW/ACM std ratio is 0.53. Both ACM components are sub-threshold in 25% of verdict weeks, and the driver flips 18% of the time. The reviewer understated the current case. KW 4w gives TP +11.2 vs expected path +15.3 with real driving, and S&P 4w is +2.019% (≥+2%, so ↑). That cell is 성장 주도 재가격, which is GREEN. So the current L1 light is red under ACM and green under KW. After the A alarm expires on 10/16, the 방어 vs 중립 state depends on model choice and a 0.02pp S&P margin. KW TP 1.07 is the highest since 2010-04, ACM's since 2014-07.
verdicts.corrected_fix: The reviewer's fix (own-threshold plus margin plus ACM-KW agreement, otherwise '혼합' (mixed) = yellow; define 보류 as yellow) is sound. Also add a hysteresis rule at every boundary, for example keep the prior verdict when a component is within 10% of its threshold. And source KW from feds200533.csv, not FRED.

verdicts.reason: The core holds. On 10/13 closes, rate-vol is MOVE 5d -3.9%, ^TYX 20d +19.9bp, ^TYX 5d -7.8bp, so green by rule. It was red on 9/28 (TYX5 +26.5, MOVE5 +25.4%) and on 9/29 (+29.1, +35.7%), and last yellow on 10/5 (TYX20 +41.9). The example's '^TYX 20일 +27bp' is the pre-open 10/14 value. DXY 20d is +2.54% on 10/13, and HYG/IEI -0.84% / HYGH -0.74% reproduce. The 방어 verdict survives (A valid, ACM-based L1 red, hedge red). Two details are overstated. The credit '+20%' is already labelled in the doc as '잠정, 정확한 20일 변화는 FRED로 확인 필요' (provisional, check the exact 20-day change on FRED), so that is disclosure, not cherry-picking. DXY 20d was ≥+3% on every day from 10/5 through 10/12 (3.04 to 3.51%), so a dollar yellow was defensible one day earlier on a DXY proxy. That fact supports the as-of point rather than refuting the example. The missing as-of/hold rule is the real defect.
verdicts.corrected_fix: As proposed: judge each light on the latest complete close, with an explicit hold of N trading days after a trigger (or state that there is none). Rewrite the example with rule metric, value and as-of date for each bucket, and mention the 9/28-29 red.

verdicts.reason: Text check: the daily list (L345) leaves out TLT and the VIX level, both needed for A/B, and bucket lights are refreshed only at the weekend (L350). Evidence beyond the reviewer's: on Fridays only, the rate-vol light was green on 9/25 (MOVE5 +19.05%, TYX5 +17.3), 10/2 and 10/9. A weekend refresh would never have shown the 9/24 yellow or the 9/28-29 red, so it brings back exactly the sampling miss v2 claims to fix. My own daily reconstruction (L1 ACM weekly, rate-vol, equity-vol, hedge, DXY-proxy dollar, A/B validity; credit, NFCI and SOFR omitted) gives 25.9 state changes a year for 2008-2025, 30 in 2025, and 30 of 84 방어 spells under 5 days. That matches the reviewer's 25/yr, 30 and 30-of-80. A weekly-upgrade variant without dwell still gives about 20 a year, so the dwell requirement matters.
verdicts.corrected_fix: The reviewer's fix is sound: evaluate daily on closes, downgrade immediately, upgrade only at the weekend review after 5 trading days in the better state, 방어 takes precedence. Complete the daily input list (HYG, IEI, TLT, MOVE, DXY, VIX, VIX3M, ^TYX).

verdicts.reason: The numbers reproduce. S&P-TLT 63d correlation in 2026: red 63%, yellow 35%, green 2%; in 2025: 6/63/31. Since July 2026 it was red 97% of days (min 0.27). Real-rate 3y percentile has been ≥94.1 every week since 7/3 and ≥95 since 7/10. The framing is weak, though. Principle 2 says to show level and speed side by side, not that levels are irrelevant, and Layer 2's question explicitly asks 'how thick is the cushion', which is a level concept. A bond leg that no longer hedges is a legitimate sizing input. Calling 공격 'unreachable' also overstates it: it held on about 18-23% of 2026 days in both my reconstruction and the reviewer's. The stronger version of this critique is double counting: real-rate level (L1 red) and positive stock-bond correlation co-move in a rates-led regime, which conflicts with principle 1.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Do not demote the hedge bucket outright. Either cap level-driven reds (L1 red via the percentile, hedge red via the correlation level) at one combined red, or state explicitly that '공격 requires bonds to hedge' as an intended design choice. Speed-based variants can be added as yellow triggers.

verdicts.reason: Daily rolling rule, 2008 to 10/13. On load()'s calendar I get A: 48 days / 21 episodes (10-day gap) with episode-start 63d MDD median -4.1% and P(<-10%) 30%. B: 120 / 39, median -3.1% (unconditional -3.0%), P 23% (unconditional 15%). A or B valid on 16.9% of days. The reviewer reported 46/19, -4.7%, 33%, 109/36 and 15.6%. The exact counts depend on episode definition, but the conclusion holds: the rule actually run fires more often with a weaker edge than the quoted weekly 12-week/-5.7%/42% figures, and B's median edge is about zero. The doc does label those stats '주간 기준' (weekly basis), so they are transparent, but they describe a different rule. Phantom confirmed: on load()'s ffilled calendar B fires only on 2026-02-16 (Presidents' Day). On a trading-day calendar 2/13 fails (VIX 5d +1.1%) and 2/17 fails (MOVE 5d +9.72%), so B never fires in 2026. There is a further calendar mix: on 10/12 (bond holiday) ^TYX printed 5.598 and TLT/^GSPC traded, but ^MOVE had no print and was forward-filled.
verdicts.corrected_fix: As proposed: backtest the exact daily rule and report episodes. Build the calendar from NYSE trading days and drop non-trading rows before differencing (do not ffill holiday rows). Define 10영업일 as the 10 NYSE trading days after the firing day. Also report B's weak median edge alongside A's.

verdicts.reason: Facts confirmed. yahoo.csv mtime is 13:28:57 UTC on 10/14 (09:28 ET). The raw 10/14 row has only ^MOVE 96.65, ^TNX, ^TYX 5.621, ^VIX 15.80, DXY 102.835 and BTC, and the ETFs and ^GSPC are forward-filled. Hybrid vs 10/13 close: TYX 5.621/99.4/z 1.21/+27.2bp vs 5.563/98.7/0.86/+19.9. MOVE 96.6/58/1.15 vs 101.1/67.7/1.24. VIX/VIX3M: the hybrid is 0.88 (pct 53, z -0.20) vs 0.85 at close (pct 27.6, z -0.47). S&P-TLT 0.454 vs 0.425. DXY since 8/19 +4.05% vs +3.39%. The 30Y closing high was 5.665% on 10/5. However, none of these changes a light or the verdict, and the doc says '10월 13~14일 값' (values from 10/13-14). The one substantive knock-on is that '30년물 5.62% … 2002년 6월 이후 최고' (30Y 5.62%, highest since June 2002) is not even the 2026 closing high.

verdicts.reason: My independent classifier gives exactly 109 of 1189 undefined weeks: 91 flat-nominal with real-rate change within ±20bp (41 BE↓, 50 BE↑), and 18 falling-rate, expected path × real, S&P →. Two of those weeks are recent (2026-06-12 and 06-26). The completeness claim at L84 is therefore false. I lower it to medium because a default (undefined = yellow) is obvious, the gap affects one bucket by one step about 5 weeks a year, and the fix is a few rows.

verdicts.reason: The core is right. verdicts.reason: Verified: 432 lines and 14,864 characters. Page 1 is the v1 changelog (L11-23), and the verdict is at L336 (78%). 35 of 58 code-block lines exceed 40 display columns (max 83), and the longest cell is 179 columns at L90. One caution on the fix: an 'auto-generated status card' needs a data pipeline, and a static page would show a dated snapshot. The key editorial fix is to separate stable rules from dated readings. Both an artifact and a self-hosted page support collapsible sections, so the structure argument does not by itself favour one over the other.

missed: Knife-edge readings with no hysteresis. The current 4-week S&P is +2.019% against a ≥+2% bar, and 9/11 nominal was +19.88bp against ±20. Under KW the S&P margin alone flips the current L1 light from red to green. Inequality wording is also mixed: 'N 안' / '넘으면' / '이상' (≥) / '초과' (>). The doc needs a boundary rule, for example carry the prior verdict within a 10% band, plus consistent ≥ / > semantics.

The B alarm's quoted evidence is selective. The doc reports A's edge (-5.7% vs -2.1%, 42% vs 12%) but omits B's weaker weekly stats in verify_out2 (-2.9% vs -2.1%, 22% vs 12%; 13-week S&P +2.16% vs +2.34% unconditional). It names 8 famous B episodes out of 23 and leaves out weak ones such as 2015-01-02, 2016-11-04, 2019-03-22 and 2021-11-26. Yet B alone forces 방어 for 10 days.

Proxy ambiguity: the indicator table allows 'HYG/IEI 또는 HYGH' (either) as the daily credit proxy, but the alarms hard-code HYG/IEI. The two diverge (8/28 to 10/1: HYG/IEI -0.85% vs HYGH -1.24%), so the choice can change whether the -0.5% leg fires. Pick one.

The MOVE>126 note says S&P was '고점 대비 10% 이상 하락' (down 10% from its high), but verify_v1.py measures from the 252-day rolling high, not the all-time high. The label should read '52주 고점' (52-week high).

load()'s weekday ffill(limit=3) also forward-fills ^MOVE across bond-market-only holidays: on 10/12, ^TYX and TLT printed but MOVE did not. So MOVE's 5-day window spans 4 real observations around SIFMA holidays, which biases MOVE 5d % in both the alarms and the rate-vol light. This compounds the calendar issue in finding 06.

result.summary:
Built v2's sizing rule daily on the cached data from 2007-05 to 2026-10, with proxies for the inputs FRED would normally supply. On the S&P 500 it beats buy-and-hold on risk-adjusted terms. Sharpe goes from 0.53 to 0.67 and max drawdown from -56.8% to -35.5%, at about 0.9pp lower CAGR and 80% average exposure. A 15% vol target gets the same result: Sharpe 0.67, drawdown -34.9%, CAGR +8.3% vs +8.0%. It changes exposure with a third of v2's turnover (2.6 vs 8.7 per year), and the alarm-only rule also reaches Sharpe 0.67. The six-light count does not earn its complexity:
- Most of v2's edge comes from the A/B composite alarms, and those thresholds were fitted on the same 2008+ data. Alarms alone, without the light count, cause 53% of the raw 방어 days.
- The count without the alarms (Sharpe 0.62) is about as good as a 200-day trend filter (0.63).
- The equity-vol light hurts: removing it lifts Sharpe to 0.71 and CAGR by about 1pp.
- The funding light never turns red, because NFCI and SOFR−IORB are unavailable.
- The hedge, layer-1 and MOVE>126 lights act as slow regime flags rather than alarms. The hedge light was red on 96% of days since 2026-05-01.
- The state flips about 27 times a year, and the one-step-up rule does almost nothing when checked daily.
- For BTC the macro state adds nothing: Sharpe 1.11 vs 1.10 buy-and-hold and 1.10 for a constant 81%. BTC's own 200-day trend filter does better (1.19, drawdown -72% vs -80%).

One thing works well: the 100/70/40 mapping matches the volatility seen in each state. Realized next-day vol is 12.6% / 19.5% / 32.0%, which implies 100/65/39. Taken literally, the rule has been 방어 since 2026-09-25 and stays there after the A alarm expires on 10/16, as long as both the layer-1 and hedge lights stay red.
result.method:
Python script (pandas 3) that loads data with analysis/verify_v1.py load(): importlib, no bytecode written, repo untouched. It uses the weekday grid with ffill(limit=3).

**Layer 1**
- Weekly on Fridays, per v2's '주 1회'.
- 4-week changes of GSW SVENY10 (nominal), TIPSY10 (real), BKEVEN10 (BE), ACMTP10 and ACMRNY10, plus the ^GSPC 4-week return.
- Implemented with v2's literal thresholds and tables (±20/15bp, ±2%).
- Two undefined cells needed a choice. When nominal is flat and BE moves, I classified by BE sign. When nominal falls driven by expected path and real yields with S&P flat, I called it green, and tested yellow as a variant.
- Red = yellow verdict and 10y real ≥ its trailing 756-day 95th percentile (past data only).

**Layer 2 (daily)**
- Credit: HYG/IEI 20-day log change, with yellow ≤ -1.5% and red ≤ -3.0%. The base mapping comes from a spread duration of about 3.5 × a 15%/30% move at roughly 300–400bp, net of carry.
- Credit sensitivity tests:
  - -0.5/-1.0 (anchored on 2026, when HY OAS rose about 25% and HYG/IEI moved -0.85%)
  - -1.0/-2.0 and -2.0/-4.0
  - -4.0/-7.5, an assumed frequency match
  - plus two versions of the HY OAS > 450 level condition: a HYG/IEI 252-day drawdown proxy, and an approximate calendar written from memory.
- Rate vol: MOVE 5-day ≥ +20% or ^TYX 20-day ≥ +40bp is yellow. Red is ^TYX 5-day ≥ +25bp together with MOVE 5-day ≥ +20%, or MOVE > 126.
- Equity vol: VIX/VIX3M above 0.95 is yellow, above 1.0 is red.
- Hedge: 63-day correlation of ^GSPC and TLT log returns, above 0 yellow, above 0.3 red.
- Funding: DXY 20-day change ≥ +3% is yellow; there is no red input. I also tested +4%.
- Composites A and B use 5-day log changes exactly as in verify_v1. They stay valid for the firing day plus 10 business days, which reproduces the 9/28, 9/29 and 10/2 A firings and validity to 10/16.

**State and exposure**
- 방어 if 2 or more reds or a composite alarm is valid; 중립 if exactly 1 red or 2 or more yellows; otherwise 공격.
- One-step-up rule, then exposure of 100/70/40 (also 100/60/20).
- Exposure for day t+1 uses the state at close t (1-day lag; 2-day lag also tested).
- Cash earns 0%, Sharpe uses rf=0, and there are no costs (a turnover×cost drag is shown separately).
- Assets: ^GSPC price index (SPY total return as a check), and BTC-USD on the weekday grid from 2015-04.

**Baselines and tests**
- Baselines: buy-and-hold; 200-day MA (100/40, on the asset's own calendar); 15% vol target (min(1, 15%/rv20), plus a 60% target for BTC); composite-only (40/100); a constant exposure equal to v2's average; and the vol target capped at 40% while a composite is valid.
- Leave-one-bucket-out and leave-composite-out ablations.
- Sensitivity runs for credit mapping, funding, layer-1 cadence, weekly conclusion, lag, mapping, T-bill cash and total return.
- Results by episode and by calendar year.
- Structural-red statistics by bucket: red runs, share of red days in runs of 20 and 63 days or more.
- Forward risk by state: forward 21-day vol and 63-day max drawdown, also within terciles of trailing vol.
- Next-day mean and variance by state.
- A circular-shift placebo (1000 shifts).
- A stationary block bootstrap (mean block 63 days, 1000 reps) of the Sharpe difference vs buy-and-hold.

key_findings.title: The six-light count adds little over simpler rules; most of the edge comes from the composite alarms
key_findings.detail:
- v2 100/70/40: Sharpe 0.67, MaxDD -35.5%, CAGR 8.0%, turnover 8.65 a year.
- A 15% vol target gets the same Sharpe 0.67, MaxDD -34.9%, CAGR 8.3%, with turnover of 2.6 a year.
- Composite-only (40% while an alarm is valid) also reaches Sharpe 0.67, with CAGR 9.8% but MaxDD -49.7%.
- Without the alarms, the count gets Sharpe 0.62, about the same as MA200 (0.63).
- 53% of raw 방어 days come from the alarm alone.
- The exposure path correlates only 0.40 with the vol target and 0.67 with composite-only, and is noisier than either.
- After 10–30bp of trading costs, v2 trails the vol target by 0.8–2.1pp of CAGR.
key_findings.recommendation: Make the core of the rule the A/B alarms plus one simple risk overlay (a vol target or the trend filter). Either show the six lights as context only, or require them to beat that core in the 6-monthly review before they count toward the state.

key_findings.title: The hedge, layer-1 and MOVE>126 lights are slow regime flags, not alarms
key_findings.detail:
- Hedge (S&P–TLT correlation > 0.3): red on 96% of days since 2026-05-01, 63% of 2026, 27% of 2023. 31% of its red days sit in runs of 63+ days, including 2026-05-06 to 09-07 (89 days).
- Rate vol: 98% of red days come from MOVE > 126 alone (74% of 2008, 42% of 2022, 32% of 2023). v2 itself calls MOVE > 126 coincident.
- Layer 1: red 39% of 2022 days.
- The literal HY OAS > 450 condition would have kept credit red for roughly 2008–2013 (approximate, unverified). In that scenario 공격 falls from 56% to 35% of days.
- Because any two reds mean 방어, two persistent regime flags pin the state: the rule is 방어 now and stays there after A expires on 10/16, as long as both remain red.
key_findings.recommendation: Count these regime-level conditions as yellow at most, or move them out of the light count into a separate slow 'posture' dial. Keep red for fast changes: 5-day and 20-day speeds, and the alarms.

key_findings.title: The equity-vol light hurts and the funding light does nothing
key_findings.detail:
- VIX/VIX3M > 1 is coincident and peaks near market bottoms. It has 143 separate red spells.
- Removing it raises Sharpe from 0.67 to 0.71 and CAGR from 8.0% to 9.0%, with MaxDD about the same (-34.8% vs -35.5%).
- Funding never turns red, because NFCI and SOFR−IORB are unavailable. With DXY only, removing it changes nothing.
- Removing credit (proxy) also slightly helps (Sharpe 0.69).
key_findings.recommendation: Drop VIX/VIX3M from the count, or use it only to confirm the B alarm. Do not count the funding light until NFCI and SOFR−IORB are actually fed in.

key_findings.title: Too many state changes; the one-step-up rule does nothing at daily cadence
key_findings.detail:
- The state changes 27.4 times a year (raw 26.4). One-step-up only inserts a one-day stop at 중립 and slightly raises the change count.
- Weekly conclusions on Fridays, with the composite still forcing 방어 on any day, cut changes to 15.3 a year. Sharpe is 0.64 and MaxDD improves to -30.4%.
- A 2-day execution lag cuts Sharpe from 0.67 to 0.62, so the result depends on acting immediately.
- For a Korean investor, each change costs FX spread and commission, and selling can realize gains taxable at 22% (above the 2.5M KRW exemption). This is not modeled.
key_findings.recommendation: Evaluate the state weekly. Require a minimum dwell (for example one step up per week, or two consecutive weekly reads to upgrade). Define each light's look-back window, for example the worst colour over the last 5 business days.

key_findings.title: The macro state does nothing for BTC
key_findings.detail:
- BTC 2015–2026: v2 Sharpe 1.11 vs buy-and-hold 1.10 and a constant 81% at 1.10. MaxDD -79.6% vs -83.0%.
- BTC's own 200-day filter: Sharpe 1.19, MaxDD -72.1%.
- v2 gave up 88pp in 2023 (+64% vs +152%).
- The proposed 7th crypto bucket has no thresholds and could not be tested.
key_findings.recommendation: Size BTC with its own trend/vol rule and crypto leverage data. Use the macro state at most as a cap during valid A/B alarms.

key_findings.title: The 100/70/40 mapping is well calibrated in volatility terms
key_findings.detail:
- Next-day S&P vol by state is 12.6% / 19.5% / 32.0%, so vol parity implies 100 / 65 / 39.
- Forward 21-day vol rises monotonically by state: 12.9% / 17.8% / 24.3%.
- P(63-day drawdown < -10%) by state: 11% / 19% / 25%.
- But v2 forecasts forward vol less well than trend or trailing vol: rank correlation -0.39 vs -0.56 and -0.58.
- Below MA200, P(drawdown < -10%) is 34%, vs 25% for v2 방어.
key_findings.recommendation: Keep 100/70/40, not 100/60/20. The latter scores better in sample but over-cuts on volatility grounds. Judge any rule change by its forward-vol and drawdown separation, not by in-sample CAGR.

key_findings.title: Gaps and inconsistencies in the spec
key_findings.detail:
- Layer 1: the cell for falling nominal yields driven by expected path and real yields with S&P flat is undefined (1.4% of weeks). The nominal-flat table only covers BE↑/real↓ and BE↓/real↑. So the claim that every case lands in exactly one cell does not hold.
- The Kim-Wright 'TP 판정 보류' (hold the term-premium call) rule has no defined effect on the light.
- The 10/13–14 worked example mixes stale or off-spec readings: rate-vol yellow from 9/24 (on 10/13 it is literally green), dollar yellow from an 8-week +4.1% (the rule is 20-day broad dollar ≥ +3%; DXY 20-day is +2.5%).
- Credit yellow is provisional: the HYG/IEI proxy moved only -0.84% while HY OAS rose about 25%.
- None of these change today's 방어 call, which rests on layer 1 and hedge being red and A being valid.
key_findings.recommendation: Fill in the undefined cells, say what 'hold' means for the light colour, and add a rule for how long a bucket reading stays valid. Recompute the worked example under those rules.

limitations: Proxies stand in for unavailable FRED data. Credit uses HYG/IEI instead of HY OAS, and the OAS-to-ratio mapping is uncertain: the 2026 anchor (+25% OAS ≈ -0.85% ratio) implies much tighter thresholds than duration math. There is no CCC−BB spread. Funding is DXY only (no NFCI, SOFR−IORB or broad dollar). There is no Kim-Wright cross-check. GSW zero-coupon curves replace DGS10/DFII10/T10YIE.
The HY OAS > 450bp calendar scenario uses approximate windows written from memory and is not verified (FRED is blocked). The HYG/IEI drawdown level proxy undercounts 2010–2013.

Everything is in-sample. The composite magnitudes were picked by the review on the same 2008+ data. Layer-1 thresholds come from the 2004+ distribution. Bucket thresholds are judgment calls that may reflect knowledge of the same history. The composite-only result is therefore probably optimistic.
One ~19-year path dominated by 2008 and 2020; few independent crises. Bootstrap 90% intervals for v2's Sharpe gain vs buy-and-hold include zero.

^GSPC is a price index without dividends (SPY total return gives the same ranking). Cash earns 0% and Sharpe uses rf=0; T-bill cash adds about 0.4pp to v2's CAGR. Trading costs, taxes (Korean 22% overseas capital-gains tax), FX spreads and KRW/USD moves are not modeled. Turnover × cost is shown only as an approximation.

The weekday grid keeps US holidays as forward-filled zero-return rows, so rolling windows count holidays. BTC's Monday return includes the weekend, and BTC's UTC close falls a few hours after the US close.
Execution is assumed at the close of the day the signal is known (1-day lag). Results get worse with a 2-day lag (Sharpe 0.62).

Choices made where the spec is ambiguous: the layer-1 undefined cells, daily vs weekly conclusion, the strict vs inclusive inequalities in the composite alarms (log changes as in verify_v1.py), and alarm validity counted as the firing day plus 10 business days.
Yahoo data quality for ^MOVE, ^VIX3M and early HYG adjusted closes was not independently checked.

issues.issue: Days with a NaN v2 state are silently dropped from v2's return series but kept for buy-and-hold, MA200 and the vol target. Cause: before 2015 the weekday grid (no BTC rows yet) has no rows for US-holiday Fridays (Good Friday, July 4, Christmas, New Year). layer1() keeps only dayofweek==4 rows, so the weekly layer-1 reading is skipped that week, and ffill(limit=5) leaves the next Mon–Wed NaN (40 days, 2008-03 to 2014-07). A ^MOVE gap in March 2013 adds 4 rate_vol NaN days. raw_state(...).where(ok) followed by apply_one_step(raw.dropna()) gives NaN exposure, and metrics() then dropna()s those 44 return days, including 2008-07-09 (-2.28%), 2008-03-26/27 and 2008-07-11. The placebo and bootstrap also apply this 'ok' mask to every strategy. result.summary:
I re-ran v2's two composite alarms on the definition v2 actually states: rolling 5-business-day changes, with episodes de-clustered on a 20-business-day gap and a 63-business-day forward window. The headline numbers v2 quotes don't hold up.

**Alarm A (rate-led)** fired in 20 episodes since 2008. A >10% S&P drawdown followed in 32% of complete episodes (6/19), against 15.5% unconditionally. The 95% CI is about 11–57%. A spaced random-date test gives p≈0.05, so A is borderline. The median 63-day max drawdown after A is -3.8% against -3.1% unconditionally. v2's "median -5.7% vs -2.1%, 42% vs 12%" comes from weekly Friday bars and does not survive.

**Alarm B (flight-to-quality)** fired in 33 episodes: 21% vs 15.5%, p≈0.22. Its median drawdown is the same as unconditional, and in 2008–2016 it ran below the unconditional rate (13% vs 18%). Neither alarm says anything about BTC drawdowns (p 0.47 and 0.17).

- **Thresholds are not the information.** Across a 500-cell grid, how a threshold set ranks in 2008–2016 has essentially no relation to how it ranks in 2017–2026 (Spearman about 0.08 for A, -0.02 for B). Still, about 90% of A-shaped cells beat the unconditional rate in each test half. The pattern (credit weak, MOVE up, TLT down, dollar up) generalises; the exact numbers don't. Moving any single threshold by ±50% keeps A between 25% and 36%.
- **A's edge is mostly the S&P trend.** When A fired with the S&P above its 200-day average, 0 of 10 episodes led to a >10% drawdown. Below the 200-day, 6 of 9 did. The current episode (2026-09-28, S&P 1.5% off its high, above its 200-day) is the first kind.
- **No incremental value over simple alarms.** In a regression on daily states, "S&P below its 200-day average" is the only indicator that survives (+20pp, t 2.4); A (+5pp, t 0.8) and B (≈0) add nothing beyond the single-indicator alarms. 90% of A/B episodes already had at least one single alarm active.
- **Bucket rules** (only the ones the cached data covers):
  - The hedge bucket points the wrong way for equity risk. When the S&P–TLT correlation is above 0.3, the drawdown rate is 4% against 15%. It is also a persistent regime flag: yellow or worse on 97% of 2026 days.
  - The rate-vol red rule "^TYX +25bp and MOVE +20% in 5 days" fired on 12 days since 2008 with no edge (8%).
  - The most informative rules are VIX/VIX3M > 1, MOVE > 126, the dollar proxy (DXY 20-day ≥ +3%) and diagnosis-red.
  - About 8% of days fall into cells missing from the layer-1 diagnosis tables, although v2 says every case maps to one cell.
  - The v2 sizing state as written separates risk only weakly. Its "defensive" state was not riskier than "neutral" on forward volatility in 2008–2016.
- **A small structural fix makes the states rank risk in the right order in both halves.** Drop the hedge bucket from the count, let A or B count as one red instead of forcing "defensive", and optionally add a trend bucket. With the trend bucket, the drawdown rate is 10% / 17% / 34% and forward volatility 12.4% / 14.4% / 22.9% for aggressive / neutral / defensive.

**Where today stands.** v2 as written stays defensive for as long as diagnosis-red and hedge-red persist. Under the fixed rule, today is defensive only because of A (still valid) plus diagnosis-red. It drops to neutral once A's 10-business-day validity expires (around 10/15–16) unless something fires again.
result.method:
I reused load() from analysis/verify_v1.py by importing it from its file path. That gives the cached Yahoo, GSW and ACM data, filtered to weekdays with ffill(limit=3).

**Sample and definitions**
- Business days are weekdays on which ^GSPC, HYG, ^MOVE or ^VIX printed. Firings are counted from 2008-01-01 to 2026-10-14.
- Alarms A and B use exactly v2's rules on rolling 5-business-day simple % changes (HYG/IEI ratio, MOVE, TLT, DXY, VIX), with ≤/≥ comparisons.
- Episodes start at the first firing. A new episode starts only after more than 20 business days with no firing.
- The outcome is the S&P 500 max drawdown over the next 63 business days, measured from the firing close: min(close[t..t+63])/close[t]−1. Only complete windows count (the last one starts 2026-07-17).
- BTC drawdowns use 7-day closes over the same calendar window. Forward 63-day realised volatility is reported as a second outcome that fits the sizing purpose.
- The unconditional rate is computed two ways: on all start days, and on non-overlapping 63-day start grids averaged over all 63 offsets.

**(1) Weekly vs daily.** I rebuilt v2's weekly Friday-bar numbers next to the daily rolling version to show where the change comes from.

**(2) Out-of-sample.** Grid of 500 cells per alarm. For A: HYG/IEI {-0.25…-1.5%}, MOVE {5…25%}, TLT {∓0.5…2%}, DXY {0…1%}. B uses VIX {5…30%} in place of DXY. On each training half (2008–16 or 2017–26) I picked the cell with the highest shrunk P(MDD<-10%), requiring at least 5 episodes, then evaluated it on the other half. I also report v2's own thresholds in each half, the Spearman rank correlation of train vs test performance across the grid, and the share of grid cells that beat the test-half unconditional rate.

**(3) Sensitivity.** Each threshold was scaled by its magnitude ×0.5, ×0.75, ×1.25 and ×1.5, one at a time and all jointly. I also dropped one condition at a time and varied the de-clustering gap (5–63 days).

**(4) Uncertainty.**
- Episode-level bootstrap (10k resamples) and Clopper–Pearson intervals for each alarm.
- Bootstrap of the unconditional rate over non-overlapping windows with a random offset, and a bootstrap CI of the difference.
- A permutation test: random start-date sets of the same size and the same >20-day spacing (5,000 draws).

**(5) Single-indicator alarms.**
- The five simple alarms got the same episode statistics as A and B.
- I checked which single alarms were already active at each A/B episode start.
- Daily linear-probability and drawdown regressions with Newey-West(63) standard errors, using 10-day "alarm active" dummies, run one at a time and all together. A and B were also tested within days where each single alarm was already active.
- A/B episodes were split by S&P trend (above or below its 200-day average) and by drawdown at the firing date.

**(6) Bucket rules.**
- Every v2 yellow/red rule that cached data can compute was evaluated daily: rate vol, equity vol, the hedge correlation, a DXY 20-day proxy for the funding bucket, and the layer-1 diagnosis. The diagnosis was rebuilt from GSW and ACM 20-day changes using v2's decision tables, with red meaning the 10-year real yield is at or above its 3-year 95th percentile.
- The sizing state was rebuilt with the credit bucket treated as green, because HY OAS is unavailable here.
- Five structural variants of the state rule were compared in each half. I also ran an exposure backtest (100/70/40%) against a constant exposure equal to each variant's average.

| State: aggressive | 57.9% | – | 12% | -3.0% | -11.0% | 12.7% | -1.6 / -3.2 |
| State: neutral | 22.5% | – | 17% | -3.2% | -13.8% | 15.4% | 0.5 / 1.4 |
| State: defensive | 19.5% | – | 23% | -3.4% | -18.6% | 15.5% | 1.6 / 2.6 |
| Defensive from ≥2 reds only (no composite) | 6.6% | – | 35% | -5.6% | -23.6% | 24.3% | 1.5 / 2.7 |

- **Hedge bucket by year:** yellow or worse on 97% of 2026 days (red 62%), and 65–70% of days in 2023–25.
- **Diagnosis gaps:** 7.2% of days have a flat nominal yield with BE moving but the real yield within ±20bp. Another 1.0% have a falling yield led by the expected path and real yield with the S&P flat. Neither case has a cell in v2's tables.

### Sizing-rule variants
Cells are P(MDD<-10%) / median forward 63-day vol for aggressive / neutral / defensive.

| Variant | 2008–26 | 2008–16 | 2017–26 | Backtest return/vol (constant exposure 0.55) | Max drawdown (constant ≈ -46%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0: v2 as written | 12/17/23%; 12.7/15.4/15.5% | 15/22/25%; 12.6/**17.8/15.7**% (not monotone) | 10/13/22% | 0.69 | -34.4% |
| C2: drop hedge, A or B counts as one red | 12/19/33%; 12.6/15.1/23.4% | 14/17/44%; 12.6/16.0/31.5% | 9/21/22%; 12.6/14.5/21.6% | 0.73 | -34.4% |
| C3: C2 plus trend red (S&P < 200-day) | 10/17/34%; 12.4/14.4/22.9% | 13/14/38% | 7/19/28% | 0.72 | **-26.9%** |

The state changes about 28–30 times a year under daily evaluation. Today (10/14): C0–C3 are defensive; C4 (C3 without the composite) is neutral.

key_findings.title: v2's headline A/B statistics do not reproduce on v2's own rolling-5-day definition
key_findings.detail: v2 quotes A as '12 weeks, median 13-week max drawdown -5.7% vs -2.1%, 42% chance of a >10% drawdown vs 12%'. Those figures come from weekly Friday bars. On the daily rolling-5-day definition v2 actually specifies, de-clustered: A has 20 episodes (19 complete), P(MDD63<-10%) 32% vs 15.5% unconditional, and a median drawdown of -3.8% vs -3.1%. The median effect has almost disappeared. B has 33 episodes, 21% vs 15.5%, and a median of -3.1%, identical to unconditional.
key_findings.recommendation: Replace the quoted stats in v2 with the daily figures and add the CI. For A: about 20 episodes since 2008, about 32% vs 15% (95% CI about 11–57%). For B: 21% vs 15%, not significant. Delete the 'median -5.7%' claim.

key_findings.title: Alarm B has no reliable edge; alarm A is borderline and fragile out of sample
key_findings.detail: Permutation p-values: A 0.049, B 0.22. The bootstrap CI of the lift includes zero for both: A [-6, +39]pp, B [-10, +23]pp. With v2's thresholds, B ran below the unconditional rate in 2008–2016 (13% vs 18%). Thresholds trained on 2017–26 give 8% in 2008–16. Only 26% of B grid cells beat unconditional in that half. A beats unconditional in both halves (25% and 36%).
key_findings.recommendation: Keep A as an information flag; downgrade B to a 'watch' note, or count it as a yellow at most. Do not describe B as a drawdown predictor.

key_findings.title: Exact threshold values carry no out-of-sample information; only the alarm's structure does
key_findings.detail: Across 500 grid cells, how a cell ranks in one half barely predicts how it ranks in the other: Spearman +0.08 for A, -0.02 for B. The cell picked as best on the training half lands at the 19th percentile (A) or 2nd percentile (B) of the grid in the test half. Yet 90–93% of A-shaped cells beat unconditional in each test half. Moving any single A threshold by ±50% keeps A between 25% and 36%. The MOVE leg matters most: dropping it cuts A to 22% and B to 17%.
key_findings.recommendation: Keep v2's round-number thresholds. Do not re-fit them every 6 months on samples this small, because that would fit noise. Freeze them and track the out-of-sample hit rate.

key_findings.title: A and B add no incremental information beyond the S&P 200-day trend
key_findings.detail: In the multivariate daily regression with Newey-West standard errors, only 'S&P below its 200-day average' survives (+20pp, t 2.4). A is +5.5pp (t 0.8) and B about 0. When A fired with the S&P above its 200-day average, 0 of 10 episodes led to a >10% drawdown; below it, 6 of 9 did. The unconditional rate is 10% above the 200-day and 34% below. 90% of A/B episodes already had at least one single alarm active.
key_findings.recommendation: Add a trend bucket (S&P below its 200-day average = red) and read A in light of the trend. The 2026-09-28 A firing came with the S&P above its 200-day and only 1.5% off its high. Historically, that kind of A firing was benign: 0 of 10, with a 95% upper bound of 31%.

key_findings.title: Hedge bucket is a persistent regime flag that points the wrong way for equity drawdown risk
key_findings.detail: On days with S&P–TLT 63-day correlation above 0, the drawdown rate is 9% against 15% (t -1.5). Above 0.3 it is 4% (t -2.5), and forward volatility is lower. The bucket was yellow or worse on 97% of 2026 days and 65–70% of days in 2023–25. It therefore uses up a red/yellow slot almost permanently. Under v2 as written, it plus diagnosis-red forces 'defensive' on its own.
key_findings.recommendation: Remove the hedge bucket from the red/yellow count. Use it only to choose the hedge instrument: when the correlation is above 0, use cash or index puts instead of Treasuries. This user holds equities and crypto, not bonds.

key_findings.title: A or B forcing 'defensive' dilutes the state; v2's sizing table is not monotone in 2008–16
key_findings.detail: Days on which A or B is still valid have a 24% drawdown rate and 14.9% median forward volatility, which is neutral-level risk. As written, v2's 'defensive' state had lower forward volatility than 'neutral' in 2008–16 (15.7% vs 17.8%). The variant that drops the hedge bucket and counts A or B as one red gives 12/19/33% drawdown rates and 12.6/15.1/23.4% forward volatility. It ranks risk in the right order in both halves (2008–16 defensive: 44% / 31.5%; 2017–26: 22% / 21.6%). Adding a trend bucket gives 10/17/34%.
key_findings.recommendation: In the sizing table, have A or B count as one red instead of automatically triggering 'defensive'. Drop the hedge bucket from the count and optionally add trend red. Defensive then means at least 2 reds.

key_findings.title: Rate-vol bucket: red cross-rule never fires usefully; yellow rules have no episode-level edge; MOVE>126 is useful for sizing
key_findings.detail: '^TYX 5d +25bp and MOVE 5d +20%' fired on 12 days since 2008 with an 8% drawdown rate. At the episode level, MOVE 5d ≥ +20% gives 12% and ^TYX 20d ≥ +40bp gives 11%, both at or below unconditional. MOVE > 126 is a coincident indicator, but it predicts forward volatility (21.6% vs 13.6%, t 2.8) and drawdowns (32%). For sizing, a coincident risk state is exactly what is needed.
key_findings.recommendation: Delete the TYX+MOVE red cross-rule and keep MOVE > 126 as red. Change v2's wording, which dismisses MOVE>126 as merely coincident, because a coincident signal is fine for sizing. Treat MOVE 5d +20% and ^TYX 20d +40bp as informational rather than counted yellows, or accept that they are noisy.

key_findings.title: Equity-vol bucket, dollar proxy and diagnosis-red carry the most usable information
key_findings.detail: VIX/VIX3M > 1: 10% of days, 33% drawdown rate, forward volatility 24.2% (NW t 3.8). Above 0.95: 24% of days, 25%, 20.7% (t 4.0). DXY 20-day ≥ +3%: 8% of days, 29%. Diagnosis-red (yellow verdict plus real yield at or above its 3-year 95th percentile): 5% of days, 29%, median drawdown -5.8%.
key_findings.recommendation: Keep these thresholds. Add forward 63-day realised volatility as a reported evaluation target next to P(MDD<-10%), because volatility is what sizing actually targets.

key_findings.title: Composite alarms say nothing about BTC drawdowns
key_findings.detail: P(BTC 63-day drawdown < -20%) is 38% after A and 44% after B, against 34% unconditionally. Permutation p-values are 0.47 and 0.17. Median BTC drawdowns are -12.9% and -14.0% against -12.5%.
key_findings.recommendation: Do not apply A/B to crypto sizing. Use the crypto-specific leverage and liquidity bucket, and state in v2 that A/B are untested or ineffective for BTC.

key_findings.title: Layer-1 diagnosis tables are not exhaustive despite v2's claim
key_findings.detail: On 7.2% of days the nominal yield is flat and BE moves at least 15bp, but the real yield stays within ±20bp; v2 has no cell for this. On another 1.0% of days the yield falls, led by the expected path and real yield, with the S&P flat; that cell is also missing. Together that is 8.2% of days.
key_findings.recommendation: Define the flat-nominal rows by the sign of the real-yield change instead of the ±20bp arrow. Add an S&P-flat case to the falling-yield cell for the expected path and real yield, mapped to yellow.

key_findings.title: Daily state evaluation churns about 28–30 times a year
key_findings.detail: In every variant the state changes about 28–30 times a year. For a Korean investor in US stocks, overseas capital-gains tax and FX spreads make that turnover expensive. Backtest return/vol is 0.69–0.73 against 0.55 for a constant exposure at the same average. That gain mostly reflects volatility clustering and does not account for costs.
key_findings.recommendation: Evaluate the state weekly, or require several days of persistence before raising exposure, alongside v2's 'one step at a time' rule. This hysteresis has not been tested here; test it before adopting it.

limitations: FRED is blocked, so the credit bucket (HY OAS, CCC−BB), NFCI, SOFR−IORB and the broad dollar index could not be tested. The credit bucket is treated as green, so the rebuilt state leans toward 'aggressive'. The funding bucket uses DXY 20-day ≥ +3% as a proxy.

Samples are small: 19 complete A episodes and 33 B episodes, concentrated in 2008, 2020 and 2022. Forward windows overlap across episodes. The Newey-West t-stats for persistent regressors (hedge correlation, 200-day trend) probably understate the uncertainty.
The trend-bucket variant (C3) was suggested by the full-sample results, so it is not truly out of sample. The half-by-half results show it is stable but do not confirm it out of sample.

The Yahoo data has gaps and forward-filled holidays (MOVE on bond-market holidays, for example). The S&P series is price-only, without dividends. The exposure backtest assumes 0% cash return and no costs or taxes.
The diagnosis is computed daily on 20-business-day changes from GSW zero-coupon and ACM data, while v2 runs it weekly on FRED par yields. ACM and GSW publication lags are not modelled.
The 2026-09-28 A episode is incomplete; the partial drawdown so far is -0.4%. The 10-day validity window is counted inclusive of the firing day, so it may differ from v2's 10/16 by one day.
The composite alarms use HYG/IEI as the credit proxy, as v2 specifies, not HY OAS.

issues.issue: The A significance test ignores how A's hits cluster in time. The 6 hits come from 4 bear markets (2008-10-10 and 2009-01-21; 2020-03-13; 2022-02-14 and 2022-04-08, whose 63-day windows overlap; 2022-08-19). The spaced-random-date null does not preserve that clustering, so p≈0.049 overstates the evidence.
issues.impact: A goes from 'borderline' to 'weak'. The direction is unchanged, but A should not be called significant.
issues.corrected_numbers: Circular-shift test, which keeps the firing clustering: A p=0.071, B p=0.213, A|B p=0.038. Year-block bootstrap 95% CI: A [6%, 54%] (reported [11%, 53%]), B [6%, 38%].

issues.issue: Outcomes are measured from the firing-day close. MOVE is published after the US close, so the earliest realistic action is the next close. Re-measuring from t+1 flips one A hit: 2020-03-13 goes from -17.5% to -6.2%, because of the +9% Friday rally followed by Monday's crash.
issues.impact: Shows that A's 32% rests on single episodes. It also widens the gap to v2's quoted figures.
issues.corrected_numbers: From t+1: A 5/19 = 26%, median -3.7%. B 21%, median -1.9%. Unconditional 15.5%, median -3.1%.

issues.issue: Saying 'A adds nothing beyond the S&P trend' overreads the additive regression. A linear model with 10-day dummies cannot pick up an interaction. The episode split shows that A still adds lift when the S&P is below its 200-day average.
issues.impact: The recommendation to read A together with trend still holds. The claim that A has no incremental value should be softened to 'no reliable incremental value; any value is confined to below-trend periods.'
issues.corrected_numbers: Below the 200-day: A 6/9 = 67% vs 33.7% base (binomial p≈0.045 ignoring overlap; 4 of the 9 episodes are in 2022). Above the 200-day: 0/10 vs 10% base (p=0.35). So 0/10 is consistent with the ordinary above-trend rate; it is not evidence that A firings are benign (95% upper bound 31%).

issues.issue: In 2008+, the hedge-bucket result rests on essentially one regime. Complete-window corr>0.3 days fall in 2023 (63), 2024 (48) and 2026 (62), with only a handful in 2021, 2022 and 2025. That makes the regressor close to a 2023–24 bull-market dummy, and the NW t of -2.5 is unreliable. I checked this out of sample on 1970–2007, using a ^TNX-based bond proxy whose sign agrees with the TLT version on 95% of days (97% for the >0.3 cut), and the direction holds.
issues.impact: The conclusion stands (the hedge bucket does not flag equity drawdown risk), but it should cite the long-history check instead of the 2008+ t-stat. In 2025, corr>0 days had a 33% drawdown rate (the tariff selloff), so the bucket is not uniformly benign.

issues.issue: v2's weekly figure is a lucky choice of weekday anchor. The script's weekly-vs-daily bridge only uses Friday bars, so it does not show this.
issues.impact: Strengthens the finding that v2's headline stats do not survive. 45% is the best of the five possible weekly phases.
issues.corrected_numbers: A on weekly bars by anchor: Mon n=10, 30%; Tue n=9, 11%; Wed n=7, 29%; Thu n=5, 20%; Fri n=11, 45% (median -5.8%). B: 27–38% depending on anchor (Fri 22%).

issues.issue: The cached yahoo.csv was downloaded at 13:28 UTC on 10/14 (09:28 ET), before the US open. The 10/14 row holds pre-open ^MOVE, ^VIX, ^TYX, ^TNX and DXY values, and ^GSPC, HYG, IEI, TLT and VIX3M are NaN. load() forward-fills those from 10/13, and bd keeps the row because ^MOVE and ^VIX printed.
issues.impact: The 10/14 'current readings' are not closes (MOVE 96.6, VIX/VIX3M 0.880 = pre-open VIX over the 10/13 VIX3M, TYX 20-day +27bp, DXY 20-day). The ETF 5-day changes on that row cover only 4 days. Historical statistics are unaffected, and today's state call is unchanged because it comes from diagnosis-red plus A validity.
issues.corrected_numbers: Treat 10/13 as the last complete day.

issues.issue: The claim that exact thresholds carry no out-of-sample information is based only on hit-rate rank correlation. For B, the mean-MDD rank transfers between halves. The strict-inequality percentile also understates ranks slightly because of ties.
issues.impact: Moderate. Keep 'don't re-fit the thresholds', but say that for B the stricter cells are consistently associated with deeper average drawdowns.
issues.corrected_numbers: B Spearman (mean MDD, train vs test) = +0.50, already in the table but missing from the headline. Mid-rank test percentiles: A 20% (train 2008–16) and 27% (train 2017–26); B 4% (reported 19%, 21% and 2%).

issues.issue: 'The MOVE leg matters most' for A is not supported. The drop-one results are within noise of each other.
issues.impact: Minor. The claim does hold for B (17% vs 19–21%).
issues.corrected_numbers: A drop-one: no MOVE 22%, no HYG/IEI 23%, no TLT 24%, no DXY 27% (n 27–45).

issues.issue: The structural fixes C2 and C3 were designed after seeing full-sample results. C2's ordering in 2017–26 is weak on drawdown rate, and C4 is not monotone there.
issues.impact: The ranking claims are in-sample. The forward-volatility ordering is the more robust evidence.
issues.corrected_numbers: 2017–26 aggressive/neutral/defensive P(MDD<-10%): C2 9/21/22%, C3 7/19/28%, C4 8/26/23% (not monotone).

issues.issue: Minor implementation differences from v2 that I tested and found immaterial. The validity window uses rolling(10) including the firing day, so it expires 10/15 instead of v2's 10/16. C0 omits v2's 'raise one step at a time' rule. GSW/ACM publication lag is not modelled.
issues.corrected_numbers: 11-day validity: A|B valid share 16.2% → 17.4%, P 23.6% → 23.4%. One-step rule: C0 ratio 0.69, MaxDD -34.4% (unchanged), changes/yr 29 → 31. Diagnosis lagged 5 business days: return/vol ratios 0.66–0.71 vs 0.69–0.73, state ordering unchanged.

confirmed_conclusions: The script re-runs and reproduces its saved output exactly (identical text). Checks that came back clean: feature windows use only past data (pct_change, rolling 63-day correlation, 200-day average, 756-row real-yield percentile), and the backtest applies exposure at t+1. Weekend BTC rows are handled correctly: weekdays only for the panel, 7-day closes for BTC drawdowns. Forward windows have no off-by-one: MDD covers spx[t..t+63], FVOL uses 63 forward log returns × √252. Instrument inception dates are fine for a 2008+ sample. Cross-series dates align (lag-0 correlations: DXY–UUP 0.955, HYG–JNK 0.976, VIX3M–VIX 0.959). Yahoo adjclose is used, so there is no ex-dividend bias in HYG/IEI/TLT.

v2's quoted A statistics (12 weeks, 42% vs 12%, median -5.7% vs -2.1%) come from Friday weekly bars and do not hold on v2's own rolling-5-day daily definition. A: 19 complete episodes, 32% vs 15.5%, median -3.8% vs -3.1%. Other weekday anchors give 11–30%, which strengthens this.
B has no reliable edge: 21% vs 15.5%, p 0.21–0.22 under both null tests, 13% vs 18% in 2008–16 with v2 thresholds, median MDD equal to unconditional.
Neither A nor B is informative for BTC 63-day drawdowns: 38% and 44% vs 34%, permutation p 0.47 and 0.17.

The hedge bucket (S&P–TLT correlation) does not flag higher equity drawdown risk and is a persistent regime flag: yellow or worse on 97% of 2026 days. 1970–2007 data with a ^TNX proxy confirms the direction (corr>0: 8% vs 23%). Removing it from the red/yellow count is supported.
S&P below its 200-day average is a robust risk-state variable in both halves: 35% vs 11% in 2008–16, 31% vs 9% in 2017–26.
The rate-vol red cross-rule (^TYX 5-day +25bp and MOVE 5-day +20%) is too rare to be useful: 12 complete days since 2008, 1 hit.

About 8.2% of days fall into cells missing from v2's layer-1 diagnosis tables (7.2% flat nominal with BE moving but real yield within ±20bp; 1.0% falling yield led by expected path and real yield with the S&P flat).

v2's state as written separates risk only weakly, and its defensive vs neutral forward volatility is not monotone in 2008–16 (15.7% vs 17.8%). Counting A|B as one red and dropping the hedge bucket (C2/C3) gives a clearer ordering. This is robust to a 5-day diagnosis lag and to the one-step-up rule.
Daily state evaluation changes the state about 26–31 times a year in every variant.

Today: v2 as written is defensive because of diagnosis-red plus hedge-red. Under C2/C3 it is defensive only because A is still valid plus diagnosis-red, and it goes to neutral after A expires (10/15 by the script's count, 10/16 by v2's) unless something fires again.
overturned_conclusions: 'A is borderline significant (p≈0.05)': once hit clustering is accounted for, p≈0.07 (circular shift) and the year-block CI lower bound is 6%. Measured from the next close, A is 26% (5/19), not 32%. A is weak and fragile, not borderline-significant.

'A adds nothing beyond simple alarms or trend': only the additive regression supports this. Below the 200-day average, A was followed by a >10% drawdown in 6/9 vs a 34% base (p≈0.045, ignoring overlap and dominated by 2022). The fair statement is that there is no reliable incremental value, with any edge confined to below-trend periods.

'A firings with the S&P above its 200-day were benign (0/10)': 0/10 is consistent with the 10% above-trend base rate (p=0.35). It shows no extra risk; it does not show that today's firing is safe (upper bound 31%).
'Exact thresholds carry no out-of-sample information': this is true for hit-rate rank only. For B, the mean-MDD rank transfers between halves (Spearman +0.50).
'The MOVE leg matters most for A': dropping any single leg gives 22–27%, which is indistinguishable at n≈20–45.
